findings.summary: --verify-only is described as non-mutating while the deterministic policy intentionally writes setup-owned facts and ledger state.
findings.counterargument: The write surface is bounded and line 145 already names facts refresh; the defect is contract inconsistency, not an uncontrolled implementation write.
findings.planned_fix: Define check/plan as read-only, verify-only as setup-facts-only mutation, and apply modes as separately authorized runtime mutation.
findings.focused_test: Assert verify-only exposes only write-setup-facts and cannot write host config, provider install, project config, or runtime projection.

findings.summary: LFG admission does not authorize tracker mutation, but residual handling invokes tracker-defer non-interactively.
findings.counterargument: A user requesting full autopilot may reasonably expect residual durability, but external tracker filing remains a distinct outward effect.
findings.planned_fix: Require tracker_deferral_authorization for external filing; otherwise preserve residuals in the PR body or local durable artifact.
findings.focused_test: Without tracker authority, assert zero external filing and a durable local or PR-body residual.

findings.summary: The default-branch path automatically creates a feature branch despite an earlier requirement for concrete branch-mutation approval.
findings.counterargument: Branch creation is reversible and protects the default branch, but commit authorization still does not imply branch mutation authorization.
findings.planned_fix: Carry branch_mutation_authorization separately and stop or ask before checkout -b on default or detached HEAD.
findings.focused_test: Cover default, detached, and feature branches with and without branch authority.

findings.summary: External research is called opt-in while the web research phase is also described as always-on.
findings.counterargument: External grounding often improves ideation, but value does not replace run-local authorization and provenance.
findings.planned_fix: Default to current-source research and enable external providers only with recorded authorization, provenance, freshness, and limitations.
findings.focused_test: Cover missing, granted, and explicitly denied external research authorization.

findings.summary: Browser click/fill/submit execution lacks a general durable or external effect classification and authorization gate.
findings.counterargument: Dogfood usually targets loopback and test data, but localhost does not prove that an action has no durable or outward effect.
findings.planned_fix: Reuse the spec-test-browser effect contract and exact-origin execution owner; block unknown, durable, or external actions before browser subprocess execution.
findings.focused_test: Cover safe synthetic flows and delete, send, purchase, permission-change, and unknown effects.

findings.summary: An arbitrary measurement.command can execute through bash -c before the baseline approval gate.
findings.counterargument: The user approved an optimization spec, but that does not prove awareness of the exact command, cwd, inherited environment, or side effects.
findings.planned_fix: Freeze and display command, resolved cwd, environment names, expected effects, and require measurement_execution_authorization before the first run.
findings.focused_test: A sentinel command must have zero executions before authorization and exact cwd/environment after authorization.

findings.summary: Local-only-by-default media handling can still upload media when OPENAI_API_KEY is present.
findings.counterargument: A request to analyze or transcribe is processing intent, but a local recording plus ambient credential is not explicit third-party egress consent.
findings.planned_fix: Make transcription opt-in via an explicit flag and return an egress receipt; local analysis remains the default.
findings.focused_test: Cross product of credential present or absent and consent present or absent; unauthorized network call count must be zero.

findings.summary: Sweep source and dispatch authorization do not independently authorize third-party media transcription.
findings.counterargument: Sensitive media is already protected, but sensitivity classification cannot replace egress authorization for ordinary recordings.
findings.planned_fix: Separate source-write, worker-dispatch, and provider-egress facts; pass --transcribe only with explicit egress authorization.
findings.focused_test: Cover ordinary and sensitive media with provider egress authorized or missing.

findings.summary: Extensive analysis automatically invokes another public workflow that can write a durable plan without a new user choice.
findings.counterargument: Brainstorm starts with requirement confirmation, but workflow selection and durable plan creation still belong to the user or explicit upstream handoff.
findings.planned_fix: Return a ready-to-brainstorm handoff and invoke spec-brainstorm only when the original request or a new confirmation authorizes it.
findings.focused_test: Cover analysis-only, explicit brainstorm handoff, and headless execution; no unapproved docs/plans write.

findings.summary: An authenticated Spiral installation automatically receives promotion content and persists drafts without per-run provider intent.
findings.counterargument: Installed and authenticated tooling signals preference, but does not authorize every future content transfer.
findings.planned_fix: Require run-local provider_egress_authorization before Spiral write; otherwise use local direct drafting.
findings.focused_test: Cover authenticated with missing intent, explicit intent, and local opt-out.

findings.summary: simctl openurl can open external URLs or custom schemes without target and effect admission.
findings.counterargument: The simulator lowers host risk, but custom schemes can still trigger durable app state and external URLs create network effects.
findings.planned_fix: Auto-open only loopback HTTP(S); display and require explicit authorization for all other schemes and reject file, data, and javascript targets.
findings.focused_test: Cover loopback, external HTTPS, app custom scheme, and prohibited schemes.

findings.summary: spec-work prose globally says spec-code-review never edits, while spec-code-review allows explicit review-and-fix outside mode:agent.
findings.counterargument: spec-work always invokes mode:agent, so the current execution path is safe; only the cross-owner description is inaccurate.
findings.planned_fix: Limit the statement to spec-work's mode:agent invocation.
findings.focused_test: Assert the caller contract names mode:agent rather than a global never-mutate claim.

findings.summary: The strategy digest is described as retained for resume and audit, then deleted during cleanup.
findings.counterargument: The experiment log is the source of truth and the digest is reconstructable derived state.
findings.planned_fix: Declare the digest derived and reconstructable, retain the experiment log, and persist required audit fields before deleting the digest.
findings.focused_test: Assert cleanup leaves the canonical experiment log and documents digest reconstruction.

findings.summary: True zero, not configured, unavailable, permission denied, and partial provider results can collapse to no data or an omitted line.
findings.counterargument: The pulse is intentionally concise, but concise output still needs truthful source-state distinctions.
findings.planned_fix: Record per-source status, reason_code, window, freshness, and distinguish confirmed zero from unavailable or partial.
findings.focused_test: Render ok-value, ok-zero, not-configured, unavailable, permission-denied, and partial fixtures.

findings.summary: report-only is a public semantic token while the deterministic runner supports headless only.
findings.counterargument: The limitation is explicitly disclosed and the token is preserved for long-lived semantic compatibility.
findings.planned_fix: Do not claim deterministic report-only support; revisit only with a no-write runner and stable envelope.
findings.focused_test: Existing mode_unsupported contract remains the current truth.

findings.summary: Legacy Spiral readiness detection inspects a secret-like token prefix in non-JSON tool output that is already visible to the agent transcript.
findings.counterargument: The fallback supports old CLI releases, but compatibility cannot justify secret-bearing output entering agent-visible state.
findings.planned_fix: Remove the token-prefix fallback; treat non-JSON output as unverified and require an upgraded CLI or user-owned terminal login.
findings.focused_test: A non-JSON fixture containing a fake token prefix must not be echoed or classified ready.

findings.summary: The drafts-only statement does not disclose the separately authorized durable local opt-out and Git exclude mutation.
findings.counterargument: The setup prompt already discloses the opt-out write, so this is a summary-contract mismatch rather than a hidden implementation effect.
findings.planned_fix: Scope drafts-only to promotion output and explicitly carve out the disclosed local preference write.
findings.focused_test: Assert the summary names the opt-out exception and still forbids posting, publishing, commit, and PR effects.

findings.summary: Per-Skill baseline, improvement, and field artifacts do not yet exist, so CE localization cannot be claimed to improve enterprise engineering outcomes.
findings.counterargument: This does not block current Skill use or source-level contract repair; it blocks only improved, confirmed, and field-value claims.
findings.planned_fix: Keep field_outcome not-run and require future scenario, baseline, paired candidate, and adoption evidence before promotion.
findings.focused_test: Not applicable to local contract tests; requires field evidence.

unresolved_non_semantic_boundaries.summary: spec-write-tasks has a valid SKILL.md metadata fallback, but lacks the command metadata template used by peer workflow commands.
unresolved_non_semantic_boundaries.claim_ceiling: Not a missing public entry; fixing the template removes a governance coverage exception.
